add.k: The founder of Skull Mesa, a haven for mutants
st: In season 4, Dr. Prescott, who once stood up for the young Scott, is freed from Solarr's paralysis when Skull Mesa turns on Solarr.

files.notes: Secrets, Not Long Buried (Wikipedia #52, S4). Named on screen ('Taylor Prescott', 'Dr. Prescott'); he speaks in the scenes with the young Scott and after he is revived. The town is a community, not a named organization, so Independent. Episode numbers follow Wikipedia's overall order, which the existing fox-anim ep tags use.

add.k: An Irish fire mutant held by Dr. Essex
st: In season 5, in Victorian London, Flannery is shown off by Essex as a test subject, then flees when James Xavier frees him.

files.notes: Descent (Wikipedia #75, S5). Essex calls him 'Mr. Flannery' and he says 'Flannery, sir. Thomas Flannery' to James Xavier; he says he left Ireland to find work during the famine. Held captive, not a member of any group: Independent.

add.k: A mutant traitor sent back in time by Master Mold
st: In season 4, Fitzroy kills Xavier in 1959 for Master Mold, then learns Master Mold will betray him and helps undo the murder.

files.notes: One Man's Worth parts 1 and 2 (Wikipedia #54-55, S4). Only 'Fitzroy' is said ('the mutant traitor, Fitzroy'); 'Trevor' is never said, so n is Fitzroy. He is a one-job hire of Master Mold, so Independent. Recap-only in Beyond Good and Evil part 1, left out. Status Allied because his recorded warning makes his past self spare Xavier and leave.

add.k: The scientist who bonded adamantium to Logan's bones
st: In season 2, in Logan's memories, the Professor oversees the adamantium bonding of his skeleton, until Logan breaks loose.
In season 4, his old tapes show Logan and Sabretooth their memories were faked, and his message sets the robot Talos on them.

files.notes: Repo Man (#18, S2) and Weapon X, Lies, and Video Tape (#61, S4 in Wikipedia's order; the Lotus and the Steel recap #60 is in the same season). Cornelius addresses him as 'Professor'; 'Truett Hudson' is never said, so n is The Professor. The program is never named on screen (the 'Weapon X' said in Repo Man is Logan's code name), so Independent. His fate after Logan's escape is not shown: Missing. A recap shot in Out of the Past (#28, S3), where Deathstrike speaks of Professor Oyama, is left out: the screen does not tie that name to him.

add.k: A Skull Mesa mechanic and family man
st: In season 4, Tusk, a family man who fears Solarr, will not help Cyclops at first but joins the townsfolk who turn on Solarr.

files.notes: Secrets, Not Long Buried (#52, S4): named on screen ('Tusk, Solarr wants to know if you fixed that generator coil'), talks with Cyclops about his family. His Graduation Day (#76) appearance is a silent, unnamed background cameo in the Genosha crowd (Marvel Database lists it as a cameo); the example files for this show give no steps for silent background cameos, so it has no step.

st: In season 2, as his future starts to vanish, young Tyler cries out for his father, Cable, and is safe once the plague is stopped.
In season 4, grown up, Tyler fights Apocalypse at his father's side and helps him steal a time machine, then stays behind.

files.notes: Time Fugitives part 2 (#21, S2: 'Tyler!' 'Help me, Dad!') and Beyond Good and Evil parts 1 to 3 (#63-65, S4: 'Tyler, you must understand why tonight is so important'; 'Ready, Dad?'). The Marvel Database splits the part 3 Tyler into Earth-13393, but on screen he is the same Tyler, so this one file covers him (that page is dropped). 'Clan Chosen' is never said; he fights in his father's band, so Cable's Resistance, the app's name for Cable's group.

add.k: A mutant whose power throws foes off balance
st: In season 2, in the Savage Land, Vertigo overwhelms Xavier and Magneto for her master Sinister, then fights the X-Men.
In season 4, now in Sinister's crew, Vertigo helps kidnap Jean after her wedding and fights the X-Men at the Axis of Time.

files.notes: Reunion parts 1 and 2 (#25-26, S2) and Beyond Good and Evil parts 1 and 4 (#63, #66, S4). She names herself ('Succumb to the power of Vertigo') and is named by Sinister's men ('Ruckus, Vertigo, Hairbag, move it!'). Group names follow the app's existing Savage Land Mutates and Nasty Boys (the transcripts do not say either name); tm staged with '#63' since both stages share the title string. The Marvel Database's Repo Man first appearance has no trace in that transcript and is left out.

add.k: A huge, furry strongman of Alpha Flight
st: In season 2, Sasquatch helps Alpha Flight capture Wolverine, then turns on Department H when it plans to take his skeleton.

files.notes: Repo Man (#18, S2): named by Wolverine ('I hope you missed me, Sasquatch'); 'Walter Langkowski' is never said. A Morph impersonation in Courage is not him.

add.k: The Scarlet Witch, Quicksilver's twin sister
st: In season 4, Wanda hunts Magneto with Pietro to avenge their mother, learns he is their father, and helps fight the High Evolutionary.

files.notes: Family Ties (#58, S4). Named 'Wanda' and 'Scarlet Witch'; n follows the app's name for other Wandas. She calls Pietro on 'X-Factor override frequencies' and Xavier asks if 'all of X-Factor is involved', so X-Factor. The Repo Man cameo (a Cerebro image, no name or lines) and the name on Forge's list in X-Men '97 are left out.

add.k: A Phalanx heir who fled the hive with his Lifemate
st: In season 5, Warlock flees the Phalanx to Earth, helps Beast make a virus against it, and carries it into the Phalanx core.

files.notes: The Phalanx Covenant parts 1 and 2 (#67-68, S5): 'I am called Warlock. It is not a name, but a title.' He broke from the Phalanx before the story, so Independent. At the end he asks for a ship to go home; he is not shown leaving, so Active.

add.k: A Skull Mesa mutant who stands guard for Solarr
st: In season 4, Watchdog downs Cyclops' plane and jams his signal for Solarr, then has a change of heart and calls in the X-Men.

files.notes: Secrets, Not Long Buried (#52, S4): 'Take him down, Watchdog'; 'Watchdog was able to jam his signal'; 'Change of heart, Watchdog?'. Solarr's gang is never named on screen ('Children of the Shadow' is only in the synopsis), so Independent.

add.k: A wizard in Jubilee's fairy tale
st: In season 5, in Jubilee's fairy tale, the wizard Xavier the All-Knowing tells her she is the key to the MacTaggert Crystal.

files.notes: Jubilee's Fairytale Theatre (#72, S5): 'It's Xavier, the all knowing'; he says 'Jubilee, heed my words. You are the key to the power of the crystal.'

add.k: The elder of a Japanese fishing village
st: In season 4, village elder Yoshida welcomes Logan and wants to keep paying the Silver Samurai, but his people rise up and win.

files.notes: Lotus and the Steel (#60, S4): 'Logan, this is Yoshida-san, the village elder'; the Samurai's man says 'You disappoint me, Yoshida.' No saved wiki page; sourced from the transcript.

add.k: High Priestess of the Sun God Garokk
st: In season 3, Zaladane steers Sauron into bringing Storm to the Savage Land, unleashes her power for Garokk, then turns on Sauron.

files.notes: Savage Land, Strange Heart parts 1 and 2 (#38-39, S3): 'I am Zaladane, High Priestess of the Sun God, Garokk.' She refuses Sauron's order to rally his troops ('Lord Garokk has decreed you have outlived your usefulness'). Garokk's followers have no group name, so Independent. Her fate after Garokk's fall is not shown.

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Years ago Dr. Prescott defends the young Scott from bullies and takes him for ice cream. Scott comes to Skull Mesa to find him, learns Solarr has paralyzed him, and the town's uprising sets him free.
stages.whoA: Scott Summers, the boy he once looked after
stages.whoB: His old friend, the founder of Skull Mesa

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Tusk tells Cyclops that Doc Prescott once got him out of a real jam. With Prescott paralyzed by Solarr, Tusk joins the townsfolk who throw Solarr out, and Prescott is revived.
stages.whoA: A Skull Mesa mechanic he once helped
stages.whoB: Doc Prescott, who once helped him

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Dr. Essex keeps Flannery locked up as a test subject and shows off his fire to the Royal Society. When James Xavier frees the prisoners, Flannery flees and the mob turns on Essex.
stages.whoA: Dr. Essex, who held him captive
stages.whoB: One of his mutant test subjects

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Bishop and Shard chase Fitzroy to 1959 but fail to stop him killing Xavier. In the changed future Fitzroy hands Bishop a tape, and his warning lets the travelers save Xavier.
stages.whoA: The time traveler who chases him
stages.whoB: The mutant traitor who kills Xavier

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Fitzroy plants a bomb that kills the young Xavier in 1959. On the second try, warned that Master Mold will betray him, Fitzroy spares him.
stages.whoA: The man he is sent to kill
stages.whoB: The assassin sent to kill him in 1959

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Wolverine and Storm join Bishop's hunt for Fitzroy and fight him and Nimrod in 1959. They fail, then return and keep Xavier alive until Fitzroy backs down.
stages.whoA: One of the time travelers who hunt him
stages.whoB: The assassin he tries to stop

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Master Mold sends Fitzroy and Bantam to 1959 with the Sentinel Nimrod to make sure he kills Xavier. Once the job is done, Master Mold orders Nimrod to kill them both.
stages.whoA: Master Mold and Nimrod, who hire and betray him
stages.whoB: Their mutant assassin

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: The Professor has adamantium bonded to Logan's skeleton, and Logan breaks loose. Years later Logan finds his tapes and learns his memories were faked.
stages.whoA: Logan, his first adamantium subject
stages.whoB: The Professor who turned him into a weapon

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: The Professor's tapes tell Sabretooth that his memories were planted and that he was next for the adamantium process. His recorded message sets the robot Talos on him and Logan.
stages.whoA: One of his conditioned test subjects
stages.whoB: The Professor who faked his memories

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Cyclops asks Tusk for help against Solarr, but Tusk is afraid for his wife and children. When Solarr tries to make an example of Cyclops, Tusk joins the townsfolk who turn on him.
stages.whoA: The X-Man who asks him for help
stages.whoB: A Skull Mesa mechanic who finally stands up

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Tyler cries out for his father as their future starts to vanish, and Cable finds him safe once the plague is stopped. Grown up, Tyler fights Apocalypse beside Cable and helps him steal a time machine, then stays behind.
stages.whoA: His father, Cable
stages.whoB: His son, Tyler

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Tyler joins his father's attack on Apocalypse's pyramid in 3999. After Apocalypse steals Cable's time device, Tyler helps him go after him in the past.
stages.whoA: Apocalypse, the tyrant of his time
stages.whoB: One of Cable's fighters

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Vertigo brings the captive Xavier and Magneto to her master Sinister in the Savage Land. Later, in Sinister's crew, she helps kidnap Jean and fights for him at the Axis of Time.
stages.whoA: Sinister, her master
stages.whoB: One of his followers

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: In the Savage Land Vertigo overwhelms Xavier and Magneto and takes them to Sinister. She fights again when the X-Men break into Sinister's base.
stages.whoA: A captive she takes to Sinister
stages.whoB: A Savage Land mutant who captures him

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Vertigo tries to force Wolverine to his knees in the Savage Land, but he gets away. She fights the X-Men again when Sinister's crew kidnaps Jean.
stages.whoA: An X-Man who escapes her power
stages.whoB: A mutant who makes his head spin

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Vertigo is one of Sinister's crew who snatch Jean after her wedding. She turns her power on the X-Men when they come for Jean.
stages.whoA: The bride she helps kidnap
stages.whoB: One of her kidnappers

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Sasquatch helps Alpha Flight bring their old teammate Wolverine back to Department H. When General Chasen orders Wolverine's skeleton removed, Sasquatch and the team turn on the general.
stages.whoA: His old Alpha Flight teammate
stages.whoB: An old Alpha Flight teammate

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Wanda and Pietro lure Magneto into a trap to avenge their mother, until the High Evolutionary reveals that Magneto is their father. They fight together to escape, and Wanda leaves unsure if she can forgive him.
stages.whoA: Magneto, the father she never knew
stages.whoB: His daughter, the Scarlet Witch

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Warlock saves Beast from the Phalanx and asks for his help to find his Lifemate. Together they make a virus, and Warlock calls him Self-friend Hank before carrying it into the Phalanx core.
stages.whoA: Self-friend Hank, who helps him
stages.whoB: A Phalanx rebel he befriends

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Forge works with Warlock and Beast against the Phalanx. At the end Warlock asks Self-friends Hank and Forge to help him build a ship home.
stages.whoA: A Self-friend who helps him
stages.whoB: An alien ally against the Phalanx

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Warlock flees the Phalanx rather than merge with it, and it follows him to Earth and takes his Lifemate. He lets the Phalanx take him so the virus reaches its core.
stages.whoA: The hive mind he fled
stages.whoB: Its runaway heir

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: On Solarr's order Watchdog brings down Cyclops' plane, cuts off his powers and jams his signal. When the town turns on Solarr, Watchdog salvages a transmitter and calls the X-Men in.
stages.whoA: The X-Man he shoots down
stages.whoB: Solarr's guard who later calls for help

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: In Jubilee's fairy tale, the wizard Xavier appears to the warrior Jubilee after she wins a piece of the MacTaggert Crystal. He tells her she is the key to its power once the two halves are joined.
stages.whoA: The warrior he tells of the crystal
stages.whoB: The wizard who guides her quest

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Yoshida welcomes Logan to the village since Master Oku has. He wants the village to keep paying tribute, but Logan backs the villagers who fight and beats the Silver Samurai.
stages.whoA: Logan, the outsider Oku welcomes
stages.whoB: The village elder

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: The Silver Samurai's men demand tribute from Yoshida's village and mock him for not controlling his people. When the villagers rise up, Logan beats the Samurai.
stages.whoA: The bandit lord his village pays
stages.whoB: The elder of a village he squeezes

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Zaladane saves Sauron from Ka-Zar and tells him to fetch Storm for her power. Once Garokk wakes, she refuses Sauron's orders and Garokk turns on him.
stages.whoA: The tool she uses to free Garokk
stages.whoB: The priestess who sends him for Storm

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Zaladane has Sauron bring Storm to the Savage Land and helps strip away her self-control. Storm's unleashed power wakes Garokk.
stages.whoA: The weather witch she uses
stages.whoB: The priestess who unleashes her

dropped.why: Same person on screen as Tyler (Earth-121893): the Tyler who helps Cable steal the time machine in Beyond Good and Evil part 3 continues the part 2 scenes with nothing marking a different timeline, so he is covered by fox-anim-tyler.

changes.where: add.st[1] and ep 'X-Men: The Animated Series|1'
changes.was: ["In season 5, Tusk is among the mutants who flock to Genosha as Magneto readies a war on humanity.", "X-Men: The Animated Series", "Active"] ; ep 76
changes.why: In Graduation Day Tusk is only a silent background cameo in the crowd on Genosha (no lines, not named). The show's example files (Apocalypse, Storm) give steps only for scenes where the person acts in the story, never for silent background cameos, so the step goes.
